newsitem.title: UK: Downturn clouds Lloyd's of London outlook -report.
newsitem.headline: Downturn clouds Lloyd's of London outlook -report.

text.p: The outlook for Lloyd's insurance market is unattractive for 1997 and 1998, with little prospect of an upturn in premium rates until 1999 or 2000, a new report said on Thursday.
"Prospects for the 1997 account cannot be good. Well into the fourth year of the down-phase of the insurance cycle there are few signs of even an incipient recovery."

The report, Lloyd's Market Results and Prospects 1997, was compiled by the Association of Lloyd's Members and Financial Intelligence & Research Ltd. Some 7,000 Names, Lloyd's traditional backers, belong to the ALM.
Like other insurers, Lloyd's has seen most rates fall from a cyclical peak in 1993.
Claims experience in most classes has been below average since then, allowing most insurers to remain in profit, but at the same time adding to the downwards pressure on rates.
"Unless trading conditions improve sharply, and there are no signs that this is probable, both the 1997 and 1998 accounts are likely to be worse than 1996," the report said.
With no major catastrophes this year, the best return that Lloyd's investors can hope for "is something less than the modest six percent return to be expected for 1996," it added.
The review section of the book looks in detail at Lloyd's insurance syndicates and agents. It also ranks syndicates by highest paid underwriter and profitability.
